newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire denies Mobutu gave Clinton departure pledge.
newsitem.headline: Zaire denies Mobutu gave Clinton departure pledge.

text.p: Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko has not told U.S. President Bill Clinton in a letter that he is willing to resign, Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda said on Monday.

The day after failed peace talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila aboard a South African navy ship, Kamanda told state television there was no truth in media reports about the contents of Mobutu's letter to Clinton last week.

"President Mobutu, to my knowledge, has never written to President Clinton to inform him of his readiness to resign. This smacks more of press speculation, particularly of a certain press which is manipulated, than of reality," Kamanda said.

The New York Times reported on Friday that Mobutu, 66, had written to Clinton saying he was willing to resign, giving way to Kabila's Alliance which has seized most of the country in a seven-month offensive.
The first Mobutu-Kabila encounter, on Sunday aboard the South African navy supply ship Outeniqua, ended with a brief communique which revealed no shift in either side's position.
Some government officials said earlier Mobutu signalled clearly in the communique he would not seek re-election after 32 years in power, portraying this as a major concession.
Kamanda, who was advising Mobutu during the talks at the Congolese port of Pointe Noire, implied the cancer-stricken president had not ruled himself out of a future election race.
Mobutu was willing to hand over to an elected successor if he, Mobutu, decided it was inopportune to run, Kamanda said.

Kamanda said the main benefit of the 90-minute talks on the Outeniqua was that each side's position was clear. Zaire was ready to attend the next round of talks which South African President Nelson Mandela said would be within eight to 10 days.
Mobutu returned to Kinshasa on Monday.
